Subject: Private Offer request - 3yr prepay / phased billing

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the call earlier. Acme Health is interested in moving forward with a private marketplace offer for Azure. Our procurement constraints: we require a 3-year committed agreement with annual prepayment (we prefer year-by-year invoicing aligned to our fiscal year) but are open to a phased prepay cadence if it improves pricing. Key asks:
- Term: 3 years (start Jan 1, 2027)
- Billing: annual prepay preferred; open to 50/30/20 split across years if that enables a better discount
- Marketplace: must be a private offer through Azure Marketplace with seller-managed billing and a single SaaS SKU
- SLA credits and auditability (SOC2 evidence) are required in contract

Attached is our procurement checklist and standard PO language. Please send a proposed private-offer structure and the expected discount schedule (term discounts, ramp credits). We need internal CFO approval by Dec 23.

Best,
Asha Mehra
Head of Procurement, Acme Health
procurement@acmehealth.com

- Committed ARR (list price equivalent): $3,000,000 over 3 years

Kim / team —

My take after a quick margin run and marketplace fee calc: we can tighten the Year1 pricing if Acme is willing to push more prepay up front. Two options to offer (one or the other):

Option A — Strong front-loaded prepay (better for Redwood economics):
- Year1 prepay: 60% at signature
- Year2 prepay: 25%
- Year3 prepay: 15%
- Effective discounts: Year1 20% off list, Year2 12%, Year3 7%
- Add a one-time Marketplace onboarding credit of $25k to be delivered as a rebate on Year1 invoice (conditional on listing publishing within 60 days)

Option B — Balanced (lower risk for Acme, slightly less discount):
- Year1: 50% prepay
- Year2: 30%
- Year3: 20%
- Effective discounts: Year1 17% / Year2 11% / Year3 6%
- Ramp protection: 10% usage credit for first 6 months above baseline

Additional note: include a single SLA performance credit clause (max credit = 5% of monthly invoice) — helps close procurement concerns without long-term exposure.

If we present Option A as the preferred commercial (better for Redwood margin + it gets Acme a materially stronger list discount and the onboarding credit), we should be ready to sign quickly. Also add a clause that any early termination triggers a true-up for consumption and unamortized onboarding credit.

I’ll draft the redline to the private-offer PDF if you want to propose Option A.

—Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
